assumptions: Each oligo's best binding site in a genome is where it binds.
IUPAC codes in an oligo mean the breadth its designers intended.
limits: A mismatch count is not an amplification failure: its effect depends on chemistry, position and temperature.
Genomes with ambiguous bases under a site leave that oligo's denominator rather than counting.
bio.jane/contract.question: How often do a published assay's oligos mismatch the genomes circulating now, and where in each oligo do the mismatches sit?

description: Check a published PCR or sequencing assay against the sequences that are circulating now: for each oligo, where its best binding site is in each genome, how many positions mismatch, and whether a mismatch sits in the 3′ end a polymerase has to extend through. It answers the question an assay's age raises — the design was made against the genomes available on the day, and the target has drifted under it since — as a RATE per oligo with an exact binomial interval, plus the mismatch count at each position of the oligo, which is the shape a manufacturer's own in-silico inclusivity table takes. IUPAC codes in an oligo are read as the breadth its designers meant, so a position a code covers is never a mismatch; a site overlapping ambiguous bases in a submitted assembly is missing data and leaves that genome out of that oligo's denominator rather than counting as a match or a mismatch. A probe gets no 3′-end rate, because it is not extended. Graded against EMBOSS fuzznuc on every oligo of twelve published SARS-CoV-2 assays over 400 genomes.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

assay.description: what the assay is called, for the result to name.

include_subject.description: also check the node's subject (the open or wired record).

primers.description: the assay's primers, 5′→3′, IUPAC allowed. Written `name=SEQUENCE` to carry the published name.

probes.description: the assay's probes, 5′→3′. Scored the same way but with no 3′-end rule: a probe is not extended.

sequences.description: the genomes to check against: wire upstream records here, or list library document names.

three_prime_window.description: how many bases from a primer's 3′ end count as its 3′ end. 5 is the window Primer-BLAST's own specificity rule uses. In bp.

name: check_assay_decay

oligos.description: per oligo: genomes scored, genomes with a mismatch, the rate and its exact 95% interval, the 3′-end count, and the mismatch count at each position

sites.description: every (oligo, genome) site: strand, start, the mismatching positions and whether the genome could be scored

threePrime.description: how many (primer, genome) pairs carry a mismatch in the 3′-end window

worst.description: the oligo with the highest mismatch rate, which is the one that decides the assay

worstRate.description: that oligo's mismatch rate, for a threshold downstream
